doc-review-1.title: Review Meeting 1: LS & MS Dashboard Home

mtg-review-1.title: Review Meeting 1: LS & MS Dashboard Home

summary.keyOutcomes: The team aligned on moving the Language Services (LS) and Meeting Services (MS) dashboards toward full automation. The Needs attention view will only show items where the system has failed to staff a meeting. Meeting changes will sync between KCP and KMP in real time so automated staffing triggers stay accurate.

decisions.heading: Dashboard purpose
decisions.text: The Needs attention board no longer tracks general new requests; it only lists items that need a human, such as the system failing to find an interpreter or operator.

decisions.heading: Staffing automation
decisions.text: Staffing is handled by the system by default for both teams.

points.label: LS Team
points.text: New requests, including FastTrack (within 24 hours), are staffed automatically with no manual confirmation.

points.label: MS Team
points.text: Operator assignment follows the same automated logic as interpreters for consistency.

decisions.heading: Status simplification
decisions.text: Complex statuses such as New Urgent Request are removed in favour of a small set (for example Staffed, Partially staffed, Needs attention).

decisions.heading: Meeting changes
decisions.text: Changes trigger the right automated response.

points.label: Time changes
points.text: If a meeting moves within a short window (for example the same day), existing interpreters are asked by SMS, email or WhatsApp to confirm availability before new staff are sought.

points.label: Language changes
points.text: Adding a language automatically finds and offers the slot to a new interpreter.

decisions.heading: Operator integration
decisions.text: Freelance operators move into a pool like interpreters and use KMP accounts to manage their own schedules.

requirements.heading: System synchronization
requirements.text: Changes made in KCP must reflect in KMP in real time to trigger automated re-staffing.

requirements.heading: Operator criteria
requirements.text: The MS team must provide the logic for operator selection (client preferences, multi-language skills, time zones) to build the automation.

requirements.heading: Notification logic
requirements.text: Proactive email or Slack alerts are required when a meeting is imminent (for example within 2 hours) and still unstaffed or unconfirmed.

act-seed-1.title: Define the bare-minimum set of statuses for the Needs attention dashboard
act-seed-1.detail: Agree offline on the smallest set of meaningful statuses (for example Staffed, Partially staffed, Needs attention).

act-seed-2.detail: Client preferences, multi-language skills and time zones, so Engineering can build the operator automation.

ifc-ms-dash.description: Operations home page. The Needs attention list shows only meetings the system could not staff or that need a human decision.

gtm-00.question: When can Sales start talking about the revamp?
gtm-00.guidance: Only once scope and a target release window are locked. Until then, talk about direction and investment (automation, new consoles) without dates or feature promises. Agree one approved line with Product and Leadership.

gtm-01.question: What are the selling points of the revamp?
gtm-01.guidance: Translate features into buyer outcomes: fewer failed or late-staffed meetings (automated staffing), more control for producers and operators, one consistent experience across roles. Limit to three messages and validate them with two or three clients.

gtm-02.question: What do we say when a client answers 'I will wait for the revamp'?
gtm-02.guidance: Position the revamp as an included upgrade, not a new product: no migration cost, accounts and history carry over, and they would run on today's platform until release anyway. Offer early access or a design-partner seat to clients who sign now, and log 'waiting for revamp' as a loss reason in Salesforce to watch the trend.

gtm-03.question: Does the revamp change packaging or pricing?
gtm-03.guidance: Decide before any external mention. If new capabilities become paid tiers, Sales needs the price book and rules for existing contracts before Beta.

gtm-04.question: What can Sales show before release?
gtm-04.guidance: A curated demo path through the mockups (Producer and Operator consoles, dashboard), a 2 minute video and a one-pager, all framed as a preview subject to change. No access to live prototypes without a Product chaperone.

gtm-05.question: Which clients become design partners and references?
gtm-05.guidance: Pick three to five friendly accounts across segments to join the Beta and agree upfront to act as references or quotes at launch.

gtm-06.question: What training does Sales get, and when?
gtm-06.guidance: Wave 1 at Beta: the story, who it is for, what changes. Wave 2 two weeks before launch: hands-on demo certification, objection sheet and FAQ. Record both for new hires.

gtm-07.question: Which accounts are affected, and how much?
gtm-07.guidance: Segment accounts by the interfaces and roles they use (producers, operators, interpreters, integrations) and rate the change impact for each. This drives the communication plan and who gets a personal call.

gtm-08.question: Which renewals fall in the transition window?
gtm-08.guidance: Flag renewals within three months of launch so no client meets the change for the first time at renewal. Brief those accounts early.

gtm-09.question: Which clients have custom workflows or integrations to check?
gtm-09.guidance: List accounts on MS Teams, Zoom or custom set-ups and run a compatibility check before cutover. Engineering confirms each one.

gtm-10.question: When and how do we tell existing clients?
gtm-10.guidance: Staged notice: announcement about 60 days out, practical guide 30 days out, reminder a week before. Always state what changes, what stays the same and who to contact.

gtm-11.question: How do client admins and producers learn the new interfaces?
gtm-11.guidance: Short guides per role, a live webinar with recording and open office hours in the first two weeks after launch.

gtm-12.question: What is the escalation path during the transition?
gtm-12.guidance: One named contact in Technical Services per region, a response time commitment and a clear route to Engineering for blockers.

gtm-13.question: Which rules must Operations hand to Engineering before the build?
gtm-13.guidance: Operator selection criteria, the minimum status set, alert thresholds (such as unstaffed within 2 hours) and re-staffing rules for time and language changes. These are prerequisites, not launch tasks.

gtm-14.question: How will we measure success?
gtm-14.guidance: Baseline today: share of meetings staffed automatically, time to staff, number of Needs attention items per day, late or failed meetings. Compare after launch.

gtm-15.question: How is the team trained on the new dashboard?
gtm-15.guidance: Hands-on sandbox with realistic meetings, one super-user per region (EMEA, AMER, APAC) trained first who then trains their team, plus updated SOPs.

gtm-16.question: Big-bang switch or transition period?
gtm-16.guidance: Recommended: a transition. Run the new dashboard in shadow mode for about two weeks while staffing continues as today, compare the automated decisions with the team's, then cut over by region or meeting type. Set go/no-go and rollback criteria in advance.

gtm-17.question: How do freelance operators move to KMP accounts?
gtm-17.guidance: Onboarding message, account set-up support and a deadline to update availability before automation relies on it.

gtm-18.question: What is the format of the transition period?
gtm-18.guidance: A clear cutoff: meetings created after the go-live date are handled in the new system, earlier bookings stay where they are. No double entry, and a freeze around large events.

gtm-19.question: How do we support the team in the first weeks?
gtm-19.guidance: Hypercare: a daily 15 minute check-in with Engineering, a shared issues channel and a named on-call engineer for the first two weeks.

gtm-20.question: What is the story and the name?
gtm-20.guidance: One narrative for the revamp, with messages per persona (buyer, event producer, operator, interpreter). Decide whether it gets a name or version label before any material is made.

gtm-21.question: What materials do client-facing teams need?
gtm-21.guidance: One-pager, deck slides, before and after visuals, a demo video, FAQ and objection handling, plus a release notes template. Built with Sales and Client Managers, reviewed by Product.

gtm-22.question: When and how do we communicate on social media?
gtm-22.guidance: No public commitments before Beta. Tease at Beta once dates are firm, launch campaign at general availability, then client stories after launch. Lead on LinkedIn with leadership voices and product visuals.

gtm-23.question: Which channels carry the launch?
gtm-23.guidance: Website product pages and screenshots, newsletter, webinar, LinkedIn, in-product announcement and help center banner, all on the same day.

gtm-24.question: How do we prove the value?
gtm-24.guidance: Collect Beta quotes, publish one case study with before and after metrics within three months and feed results back into Sales materials.

gtm-25.question: When does Support get access to the mockups?
gtm-25.guidance: Now. Share the Claude artifacts and PRD sections so Support can plan the knowledge base structure and flag usability issues early.

gtm-26.question: When does Support get Alpha or Beta access to start documenting?
gtm-26.guidance: Alpha on staging for internal testing and first drafts of articles, Beta to validate steps and capture final screenshots. Engineering shares a known-issues list at each release.

gtm-27.question: Which help articles change?
gtm-27.guidance: Inventory Zendesk: articles to update, create and retire, plus macros. Map each to a release so docs ship on the same day as the feature.

gtm-28.question: How is the Support team trained?
gtm-28.guidance: Walk-through per role, troubleshooting guides and access to the sandbox. Support attends Beta feedback sessions.

gtm-29.question: How do we handle revamp tickets at launch?
gtm-29.guidance: A dedicated ticket tag, an escalation path to Engineering, extra coverage during hypercare and daily reporting of top issues.

gtm-30.question: How does feedback reach Product?
gtm-30.guidance: Weekly ticket trend report to Product for the first two months and a standing slot in the product review.

gtm-31.question: Who owns the launch, and what is the single calendar?
gtm-31.guidance: One launch owner and one shared timeline with Alpha, Beta, launch and hypercare dates that every department plans against.

gtm-32.question: What are the go/no-go criteria?
gtm-32.guidance: Agree measurable gates (critical bugs, shadow-mode accuracy, training completion, docs ready) and who signs off, before Beta starts.

gtm-33.question: What is the rollback plan?
gtm-33.guidance: Define what triggers a rollback, how long it takes and who decides, so Operations can switch back without losing bookings.
